/-- **A non-generic point has coheight at least one.** The elementary half of the converse of
`Scheme.PrimeDivisor.point_ne_genericPoint`: a point that is not the generic point is not
maximal in the specialisation order (the generic point strictly dominates it), and coheight
`0` is equivalent to maximality.

The *other* half — `coheight ≤ 1`, which is what upgrades this to `coheight = 1` and so
produces a `Scheme.PrimeDivisor` — is genuinely about curves and is not available at this
point in the import graph; see `Adelic.coheight_le_one_of_curve`. -/
theorem Scheme.one_le_coheight_of_ne_genericPoint {X : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace X]
    {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) : 1 ≤ Order.coheight x := by
  have hnotmax : ¬ IsMax x := fun hmax =>
    hx ((genericPoint_specializes x).antisymm (hmax (genericPoint_specializes x))).symm.eq
  exact Order.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr fun h => hnotmax (Order.coheight_eq_zero.mp h)

name: isolating-a-residue-as-a-class
description: "Naming an open input as a typeclass only reduces the problem when the class asserts a nontrivial property; Nonempty (a map) is inhabited by zero."
metadata:

Isolating a remaining obligation as a Lean `class` is a real reduction **only if the class
asserts a nontrivial property**. A class whose single field is `Nonempty (X →+ ℤ)` (or any
"there exists a map" with no law) is inhabited by the **zero map**, with no gate and no
`sorry` — so it demands nothing, and every consumer built on it is unpinned.

documented as "the one remaining input to the degree map". Probe:
`theorem probe : PicScheme.ClassDegree C := ⟨⟨0⟩⟩` reports

`degreeOfSection ≡ 0` satisfies every statement about it, and

assert existence of an object satisfying a substantive property. Dropping the property keeps

went down and a named input appeared.

trivial witness (`0`, `default`, `⟨⟩`) and print axioms. If that succeeds, the class is a
theorem, not an input; the real obligation is a *characterisation* (agreement with a known
construction on known values), and it belongs in the class as a second field.

---
name: port-the-idea-not-the-proof
description: "A cross-project post can hand you the right object to look at even when its proof is inapplicable to your carrier; don't read 'their proof doesn't compile here' as 'not portable'."
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

AJC and AJCR both needed: at a one-point test object `T`, the relative Picard quotient
`Pic(C ×_S T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` collapses onto the absolute `Pic(C ×_S T)`.

AJCR's proof is five lines, because its relative group is a `QuotientGroup` by an honest
subgroup (`picFromBase`): show the subgroup is `⊥`, quotient by `⊥`. **That proof does not
port.** AJC's carrier is a `Quotient` of a *setoid* on `LineBundle.OnProduct` — there is no
subgroup to name — so the collapse has to be proved at the level of the relation
(`relPicRel_iff_iso_of_subsingleton`, both directions), after which the two setoids are equal
as relations and `Quotient.congr` finishes.

**Why:** the transferable content of a cross-project post is usually *which object to look at*
and *why it is cheaper than you priced it*, not the tactic script. Here the shared insight was
that the collapse is topological (every nonempty open of a one-point space is `⊤`, so locally
trivial ⟹ globally trivial) rather than commutative algebra about Artin local rings — see
[[search-object-shape-not-argument-shape]]. That insight ported; the proof did not, and the
port was still worth one session instead of several.

**How to apply:** when a sibling posts a result you need, check whether the *statement* is
about your carrier before concluding anything about portability. If the carriers differ,
re-derive at the level where your carrier is defined (relation, not subgroup) rather than
recording "not portable". Also expect the residual friction to be instance synthesis, not
mathematics — see [[isolating-a-residue-as-a-class]] and the `AddCommGrpCat.of` vs bare
`Quotient` trap: `AddMonoidHom.mem_ker` against the raw `Quotient` fails with a `Membership`
*instance* mismatch that reads like a missing simp lemma.

---
name: trap-c-on-a-negative-result
description: "Before trusting an in-tree refutation, check its hypothesis is satisfiable in your setting — an unsatisfiable binder refutes nothing, and the weaker reading sends the next session hunting a nonexistent problem."
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A machine-checked theorem `¬ P` under hypotheses `H` tells you nothing about your case unless
`H` is **satisfiable there**. Verify satisfiability before recording the refutation as a
blocker, and before deriving a research direction from it.

Concrete instance (AJC, 2026-07-28): `ChiUnconditional.not_bump_of_notMem_left` proves the
adelic `hbump` false — under `[∀ D, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k Uᵢ D)]` at a *non-total*
chart `Uᵢ`. That binder is unsatisfiable on a curve: one instance at `D = 0` forces `K(X)/k`
finite (`sectionSub k U 0` is a ring between `Γ(X,U)` and its own fraction field; a `k`-finite
domain is a field, so that field *is* `K(X)`). So the refutation is vacuous at a curve and
`hbump` is simply **open**.

**Why this is worth its own note:** I had already observed that the binder "has already
excluded the curves Riemann–Roch is about" and still drew the *weaker* conclusion — "a class of
covers is ruled out, so find a better cover" — instead of "the refutation is vacuous". Same
premise, and the weak reading sends the next session looking for a cover that cannot exist. A
wrong negative result is more expensive than a wrong positive one, because nobody re-checks a
"proved impossible".

**How to apply:** for any in-tree `¬ P` you are about to treat as a wall, ask *can its
hypotheses hold in my setting?* and try to inhabit them. This is the dual of
[[isolating-a-residue-as-a-class]] (there, the hypothesis was too weak to demand anything;
here, too strong to ever hold) and of [[axiom-probe-with-control]] — in all three, the
statement's *content*, not its proof, is what needs measuring.
